summary: This note documents the ATAN2 function, which computes the inverse tangent of the ratio of its two arguments, giving the angle between the positive X axis and the ray from the origin to the point (X, Y). It covers syntax (ATAN2(<y>, <x>), noting the Y coordinate comes first), argument types, the return value in radians within [-pi, pi], usage notes on type conversion and NULL handling, and an example where ATAN2(5, 5) returns 0.7853981634. The page is a clipped reference page with navigation boilerplate, which was ignored.
one_line: Reference for the ATAN2 function, which returns the arc tangent angle in radians of a point's Y and X coordinates.
key_facts: ATAN2 computes the inverse tangent (arc tangent) of the ratio of its two arguments.
If x > 0, the expression ATAN2(y, x) is equivalent to ATAN(y/x).
The arc tangent is the angle between the X axis and the ray from the point (0,0) to the point (X, Y), where X and Y are not both 0.
The syntax is ATAN2( <y> , <x> ), and the first parameter is the Y coordinate, not the X coordinate.
Both arguments are of data type DOUBLE, and the Y coordinate is the parameter <y>.
The returned value is of data type DOUBLE.
The returned value is in radians, not degrees.
The returned value is a number in the interval [-pi, pi].
If an argument is a numeric data type other than DOUBLE, the value is converted to DOUBLE.
If an argument is a string, the value is converted to DOUBLE if possible.
If an argument is of any other data type, the function returns an error.
If either argument is NULL, the returned value is NULL.
